Change Password: the active user must first confirm the current password; the confirmation dialog masks the password, enables OK only when text is entered, compares against the current user's stored password, and then proceeds to the new/retype password dialog.

Group Policies: reusable role/permission profiles; All plus categorized permission tabs; synchronized permission selections; Select All per current tab or globally; per-permission descriptions; 117 current permissions across Main, Sales, Inventory, Finance, Reports, Setup, Settings, Tools, Shopify and Integration; assigned to users through Users Accounts.

Options: local IMS preferences for Theme (Default/Light/Dark), installed Language, and Windows printer/copy defaults for Sales Transactions, Stock Transfers, Daily Cash Report and Other Reports; Theme/Language changes can prompt an application restart; Save writes local options and an activity-log entry.
Settings: company/time-zone/maintenance/update/email/loyalty/operator/transaction configuration. IMS 9.4.4 VAT settings include enable flag, VAT Account No., Percentage and sales rounding increment.

System Dashboard: current/latest IMS and updater versions, active database/server/time zone, PostgreSQL HA primary/standby state, connection latency, active workstations, Access Log, grouped live PostgreSQL sessions and the IMS 9.4.4 Performance Monitor with Min/Max/Avg timing and Good/Fair/Slow/Critical health.

Users Accounts: global IMS identity/login/contact plus current-company Store/Supplier/Group Policy/transaction scope; new users receive current-company access; Remove deactivates current-company access rather than deleting the global identity.

Users Activity (window title System Log): audited IMS actions filtered by date, one user or All Users, and ModelsToAudit selections; results include Model, timestamp, Center, transaction no., IMS version, optional User Name, PC Name, IP address and Action Details; links to a separate Access Log viewer.

Multi-Company Architecture: global identity/company membership with independent company databases and company-local operational permissions. New company databases are created and initialized by IMS Global through Companies → Create DB; use the supported provisioning workflow rather than manual company database creation.
PostgreSQL Deployment & Operations, including the rule that company database provisioning is performed by IMS Global.
Secret Vault: server-mediated storage of sensitive credentials including company database secrets.
Secure Bootstrap: workstation check, global login, password-change enforcement, authorized company list and company database routing.
Security Architecture: workstation authorization, global authentication, Global Administrator sessions, company membership and company-local permissions.
Component Versions and Compatibility: documented versions, supported interfaces, company migrations and worker requirements.

System Dashboard & Observability: versions, active database/server, HA state, latency, workstations, sessions and transaction performance; transaction telemetry exists only where Store Debugging Mode is enabled.

Custom Attributes: define global Supplier or Store attributes; ID, Name and display Format; spaces in names are stored as underscores; values are maintained per Supplier/Store in Manage; attributes become available to Custom Reports through SupplierID/StoreID.

Custom Reports: create reports on active Custom Views; owner/name/description/active state; all-users or selected-user access; Report Fields with header, Field Type, Custom Format and None/Sum/Average/Count/Min/Max; automatic grouping when aggregation is used; Store/Supplier Custom Attributes; Order By; report deletion blocked while Reporting Scheduler tasks use it.

Custom Views: the DBA first creates an approved public-schema base reporting view named vw_*; IMS then registers it in cr_views, loads its columns, assigns one of 12 Field Types, controls Active status, and exposes it as the data-source layer for Custom Reports. Deletion is blocked while reports use the view.
Windows service scheduling, inclusive stock-movement window, maintenance state, reports, supplier-notification limits and outbound integrations.

Label Printing: Price/Sale label templates; Item/Barcode or Style entry; scanned-style/scanned-color expansion; optional selected-store positive balance as Qty; item/brand/style/color/size/prices list; Item/Qty, Style/Qty and Style/Color/Qty tab-delimited imports; Crystal Reports preview and print.

Reporting Scheduler: schedule Custom Reports by Day/Week/Month; optional TransDate period logic; required StoreID/SupplierID where-clause selection; TXT, CSV or XLSX output; file prefix/date format/remove header; Email and/or FTP delivery; server execution by IMS Autos; execution history in cr_TasksResults.
